title: ReynoldsFlow: Physics-Inspired Spatiotemporal Flow Representation for Video Understanding
abstract: arXiv:2503.04500v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Video understanding has largely relied on deep spatiotemporal architectures, including 3D convolutional networks and optical flow (OF) based models. While effective, these methods are often computationally expensive and depend on heuristic motion representations that are sensitive to illumination, scale, and structural changes. To address these limitations, we propose ReynoldsFlow, a physics-inspired representation grounded in the Reynolds transport theorem (RTT) and Helmholtz-Hodge decomposition (HHD). ReynoldsFlow decomposes motion into curl-free (CF) and divergence-free (DF) components, providing a principled and interpretable characterization of scene dynamics. By coupling intensity information with decomposed motion cues, it produces dynamics-aware, texture-preserving features that boost downstream tasks such as pose estimation, action recognition, and tiny object detection. translated_title: ReynoldsFlow：受物理学启发的时空流表示用于视频理解
translated_abstract: 视频理解在很大程度上依赖于深度时空架构，包括3D卷积网络和基于光流（OF）的模型。尽管这些方法有效，但它们通常计算成本高昂，并且依赖于对光照、尺度和结构变化敏感的经验性运动表示。为解决这些局限性，我们提出了ReynoldsFlow，这是一种基于雷诺输运定理（RTT）和亥姆霍兹-霍奇分解（HHD）的物理学启发表示方法。ReynoldsFlow将运动分解为无旋（CF）和无散（DF）分量，提供了对场景动力学的原理性且可解释的表征。通过将强度信息与分解后的运动线索耦合，它生成了动态感知、纹理保留的特征，从而提升了姿态估计、动作识别和微小目标检测等下游任务。ReynoldsFlow轻量且模块化，可以轻松集成到现有系统中。
tldr: 提出了ReynoldsFlow，一种基于雷诺输运定理和亥姆霍兹-霍奇分解的轻量级物理学启发表示，将运动分解为无旋和无散分量，以高效、可解释的方式提升视频理解任务。
en_tdlr: ReynoldsFlow proposes a lightweight physics-inspired representation grounded in the Reynolds transport theorem and Helmholtz-Hodge decomposition, decomposing motion into curl-free and divergence-free components to efficiently and interpretably enhance video understanding tasks.
